record.paper_title: Current Unsolved Problems in Planetary Nebulae Research
record.original_question: Where are the binary companions that are often invoked as the drivers of proto-planetary-nebula shaping, and if they remain undetected, are they predominantly very low-mass companions such as stars below 0.2 solar masses, brown dwarfs, or planets, or instead companions on orbital periods longer than about 30 years?

evidence.quote: Thus there is no direct evidence of a close binary companion in any of the proto-planetary nebulae.

So, we seem to be left with the following unanswered questions: Where are the binary companions thought to be the drivers of the shaping of the nebulae in proto-planetary nebulae? Are they low-mass (<0.2 Mʘ ) stars or even brown dwarfs or planets, or do they have long (>30 yr) periods?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A proto-planetary nebula (proto-PN) is the short-lived transitional object produced when a star evolves off the asymptotic giant branch toward the planetary-nebula phase. Many proto-PNe display strikingly axisymmetric or point-symmetric morphologies (bipolar lobes, jets, multipolar structures) that are widely modeled as being shaped by interaction with a binary (or substellar) companion to the central evolved star. However, no direct detection of a close stellar companion has yet been made for any proto-PN central source.

Formulate and answer the following question. Within the population of proto-planetary nebulae whose morphologies indicate companion-driven shaping:

(a) Identify, observationally, the binary companions of the central stars of proto-planetary nebulae.

(b) If such companions remain undetected by current methods, determine whether they are predominantly:
   (i) very low-mass companions, namely stellar objects with mass M < 0.2 M_sun, brown dwarfs, or planets; or
   (ii) stellar companions on long orbital periods, P > 30 yr,
or some combination of (i) and (ii), and quantify the relative frequencies of these populations.

Provide observational or theoretical evidence sufficient to discriminate among these possibilities for the proto-PN sample.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches in the planetary-nebula literature indicate that the question of the missing companions in proto-planetary nebulae remains open: although indirect evidence (morphology, jets, accretion signatures) strongly supports binary interactions, no direct detection of a close binary companion in a proto-PN central star has been reported, and the underlying companion mass and period distribution is still unconstrained.

status_evidence.snippet: Lists the absence of detected close binary companions in proto-PNe as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The question is identified as currently unsolved.
